findings.title: All 14 success criteria have corresponding tasks
findings.description: Each success criterion from the slice design maps cleanly to one or more tasks: enum creation (Task 1.1, covered by criterion 1), field addition (1.2 → 2), loader validation (1.3, 1.4 → 3-5), enforcement module (2.1-2.3 → 6-9), SimulationManager wiring (3.1-3.4 → 10-11), config defaults (4.1-4.2 → 12), regression (3.5, 5.1 → 13), and manual viewer walkthrough (5.2 → 14). No gaps.

findings.title: Tasks follow a sound sequential dependency chain
findings.description: Section 1 (config types) precedes Section 2 (enforcement module that imports them) precedes Section 3 (SimulationManager that imports both) precedes Section 4 (YAML defaults that rely on Section 1's loader) precedes Section 5 (verification). No circular dependencies. Test tasks immediately follow their implementation tasks (test-with pattern: 1.4 follows 1.1-1.3; 2.3 follows 2.1-2.2; 3.4 follows 3.1-3.3).

findings.title: Commit markers placed at working, tested points
findings.description: Five commit tasks at the natural completion points of each section. Each commit sits after a section's tests run green. None of them are bare checkboxes after every task, and the final commit at 5.5 captures docs only — appropriate for the final-doc-update step.

findings.title: Task granularity is appropriate for a junior AI
findings.description: Each task is small enough to be completed in one focused pass with a clear success criterion. The largest task is 3.4 (integration tests for SimulationManager) at ~10 lines of substeps, which is reasonable given it covers 5 distinct test scenarios plus a call-site update sweep. The Notes section at the end provides implementation rationale that helps a junior AI without dictating every code detail.

findings.title: Proportionality — task count and file count fit the slice
findings.description: 17 numbered tasks across 5 sections, 5 source/test files touched plus 2 YAML configs and CHANGELOG. This is well-matched to a slice with 14 success criteria and an Effort estimate of 2/5. Not overweight, not under-scoped.

findings.title: Implementation-dictation in Tasks 1.3 and 2.2 is justified
findings.description: Task 1.3 spells out the exact validation pattern (matching the existing `_VALID_LOG_LEVELS` style) and Task 2.2 gives the numpy semantics for `_apply_wrap` and `_apply_reflect`. This level of dictation is appropriate where: (a) the codebase has an established error-message style the slice design explicitly references, and (b) numpy semantics around `np.mod` and `np.abs` are subtle enough that leaving them open risks subtle bugs.

findings.title: Task 3.1 describes `world_bounds` as a required argument but implementation made it optional
findings.description: The task says "Add a new required keyword argument `world_bounds: WorldBoundsConfig` to `SimulationManager.__init__`". The actual implementation (src/migratory_server/simulation.py:54-58) defaults it to `None` and falls back to `entity_manager.world_bounds`. This is a benign implementation divergence — making the argument required as the slice specifies would have forced updates to every `SimulationManager(...)` call site in the existing test suite (Task 3.4 already addresses this for `test_simulation.py`, but not other test files). The implemented approach is arguably better because it provides a graceful default. Flagging as informational only since the work is complete and the task breakdown is a historical record.

findings.title: Slice design and task breakdown both describe the codebase as pre-implementation; current code already implements it
findings.description: Both the slice design and the task file are marked `status: complete` in frontmatter, consistent with the implementation now present in `src/migratory_server/config.py`, `src/migratory_server/bounds_enforcement.py`, `src/migratory_server/simulation.py`, `src/migratory_server/server.py`, `config/default.yaml`, `config/test.yaml`, `tests/test_bounds_enforcement.py`, and `tests/test_config.py`. The task breakdown correctly guided the implementation. Note: the actual codebase has gone beyond the slice's stated scope by adding a `SOFT` policy variant with `SoftBoundsConfig` and a corresponding `bounds_enforcement.py` `case BoundsPolicy.SOFT` arm, but the slice design explicitly lists `SOFT` as out-of-scope and the task breakdown correctly does not require it. This is implementation history, not a task breakdown defect.

findings.title: No NFR restatement; no load test task needed
findings.description: The slice design does not restate any non-functional requirement that would warrant a load test in `tests/load/`. The success criteria are functional/behavioral only. No missing item.
